title: Compact credential blueprint and asyncstream bridge for Python/TypeScript/Go
author: Sofia Martinez
release_notes: Introduce a compact credential preset system + asyncstream bridge across Python/TypeScript/Go SDKs. Ergonomic API improvements for token refresh and streaming consumer shutdown. Bumped python->0.12.3, typescript->1.28.0, go->v1.8.2.
description:
Motivation: Multiple small SDK changes spread across languages resulted in inconsistent credential presets, duplicate retry semantics, and divergent streaming shutdown behavior. This PR consolidates a compact credential blueprint (presets) and introduces a minimal asyncstream bridge that standardizes stream close semantics and provides a lightweight token refresh hook across Python/TypeScript/Go. The description below captures design intent, migration notes, and testing summary.

Changes: 1) Credential presets: a small, language-agnostic configuration shape (timeout/jitter/backoff/refresh-window) implemented as 'compact presets' and applied by default in each SDK. Presets are additive and opt-out; existing explicit configs continue to work. 2) Token refresh hook: a single-statement callback interface (sync/async variants) to centralize reauth flow and avoid duplicated refresh logic in stream consumers. 3) Asyncstream bridge: a thin adapter that normalizes async iterator/async generator closing semantics and exposes a cancelable close() method on stream handles. This prevents common leaks when consumers bail out mid-stream and ensures the underlying connection and credential leases are released promptly. 4) Retry harmonization: small adjustment to our default backoff floor (100ms->150ms) for the compact presets to reduce burst retries observed in high-concurrency experiments; policy remains configurable. 5) Version bumps: python 0.12.3, typescript 1.28.0, go v1.8.2; release notes included.

Migration:
- Most users will see no changes; presets are the default only for SDK clients instantiated after the bump.
- If you supply custom retry/backoff credentials, those values are preserved.
- Streaming consumers who relied on implicit GC close should now call stream.close() or use the provided async-context helpers; fallbacks remain but emit a telemetry warning for two minor releases.

Tests and CI: Unit tests added for python/ts/go around credential swap and stream close paths. Integration job runs against a small canary service to validate token exchange under churn.

Performance: Microbenchmarks show negligible overhead for the bridge (<0.6% median latency at 95th). Some spike in short-lived client churn tests decreased tail retries due to the modified default floor.

Implementation notes:
- Python: introduced sdk/python/redwood/auth/compact_presets.py and sdk/python/redwood/stream/asyncstream_bridge.py; client constructor accepts preset="compact".
- TypeScript: added packages/sdk-ts/src/auth/presets.ts and packages/sdk-ts/src/stream/bridge.ts; updated factory helpers.
- Go: added internal/cred/presets.go and internal/stream/bridge.go; exported minimal adapter on Client.StreamHandle.

Backwards compatibility: preserved. Tests: 48 new unit+integration tests across repos. CI: cross-repo matrix ensures all three SDKs build and lint. See commits for granular changes.

review_thread: Aisha Patel: Can we avoid changing the default backoff floor? We saw regressions in long-tail for heavy IO. Reply: Sofia Martinez: We tested several values; 150ms reduced burst retries in our synthetic churn tests without affecting steady-state throughput. It's configurable via presets and can be reverted per-client.
Liam Chen: TS types look fine but add a small helper doc in the factory to show how to pass a sync refresh callback. Reply: addressed in commit f6a9b54, added examples and inline doc comments.
Ravi Kapoor: Go bridge API looks idiomatic, but ensure Close() is idempotent. Reply: made Close() safe to call multiple times and added unit test asserting idempotence.
QA (Harper Nguyen): Integration flaked once on token exchange, re-ran canary job, now stable. CI logs show transient network failure on first run.
